purpose: Test whether a native photograph predicts interior features in another observation before preparing a Pallas photographic surface.
conclusions: The rigid camera formula and the archived matrix projection agree to less than 0.001 pixel on inspected points. Same-image registration is about 0.10 pixel withheld RMS.

The simultaneous camera pair still differs by 1.168 pixels withheld RMS after fitting center and roll. This measures inter-camera/processing/matching disagreement, not a calibrated physical-camera uncertainty.

Four-minute transfer improves from 3.107 to 1.470 pixels withheld RMS after a rigid fit. The 56-minute prediction gives 2.716 pixels RMS without an interior fit, and 4.372 after that fit. Neither meets the inherited matcher criteria.

Selecting reference patches that repeat within one pixel in the independent simultaneous camera pair leaves 13 reference patches and only five later-frame matches. This does not supply the required six fit and six withheld controls.
The instrument calibration hypothesis, alternative IAUspin record and quadratic illumination-removal trial do not qualify the later-frame transfer. No candidate correction was adopted.

A one-pixel threshold inherited from spacecraft filter registration is not an established SPHERE uncertainty. Failing it is not proof that photographic registration is impossible; neither the telescope PSF nor this empirical camera-pair disagreement is an absolute registration-error bound.
pixelConvention: Zero-based x right, y down; FITS rows reversed once. Native 256 by 256 float64 samples at 3.63 mas per pixel; relative detector signal, not calibrated I/F.

method.patchBounds: Projected source-mesh bounds; the original brightness threshold marks 64434 of 65536 detector pixels as foreground and does not locate this asteroid.
method.partition: Checkerboard patches fixed before each fit; withheld partitions were consulted during method selection and are not an untouched final validation set.

report.limitations: One rotation of the camera fitted to the lit limb of the retained mesh; range, focal length and Sun direction keep their source values. Residuals are along-normal limb distances in pixels; terminator and shadow edges are excluded by the mesh lighting, remaining outliers by a robust re-fit.

instrumentCalibration.interpretation: After detector preprocessing, N_CCD = theta0 - field offset, counterclockwise from image up; theta0 approximately +2 degrees and camera dependent. A raw-image camera would therefore have nominal clockwise north azimuth minus two degrees when field offset is zero. This hypothesis worsens the retained transfer and is not adopted as the released Pallas calibration.
instrumentCalibration.limitations: The exact astrometric corrections applied to the released deconvolved Pallas frames remain unverified.

reproduction.scope: Recorded match coordinates and residual statistics replayed against frozen controlled-camera formulas. These are exploratory measurements, not a production preparation recipe; full feature-search drivers remain in ignored output.

limitations: No absolute feature identities were established from the previous tentative crater picks.
A publication arrow raster is not a precision astrometric control; line width and rasterization were inspected, not converted into a confidence interval.
Method variants reuse observations and withheld partitions; a future accepted method needs fresh independent evidence.
No photographic surface, atlas, app build or browser qualification results are claimed.
